solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rebuttal arising from dispute at shop till?

definitions.note: a rebuttal is a reasoned reply opposing what someone else has claimed

parts.note: the shop counter is where the till stands and customers pay
an argument is a dispute

explanation.surface: A rebuttal that started as a squabble with the cashier.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order; 'at' simply places the dispute at the till.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a case made against an opposing claim, an opposing case.

clue.text: What we are now hearing — banks will offer these

definitions.meaning: reports of present-day events, the news being told to us at this moment
everyday bank arrangements for holding money you can draw on at any time

explanation.surface: A news broadcast followed by a remark about what banks sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Current means present, so accounts of the present are news; separately, banks provide everyday cheque accounts by this name.

clue.text: Release ladies and gentlemen held by a French female

indicators.note: held by means the toilets sit inside the French article, clasped by it

parts.note: une is the French for 'a' with a feminine noun
public toilets marked Ladies and Gentlemen are loos

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman holding a group of people, who are then let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies and gentlemen' looks like an audience being addressed; here it means the two lavatories, LOOS in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose something is to set it free, a slightly archaic synonym of release.

clue.text: Artist with studio limited by feeble brand identity

indicators.note: limited by means the pair is hemmed in on both sides by the word for feeble

parts.note: tame, as in a tame ending, means feeble or uninspiring
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a den is a small private room for work, like a study or studio

explanation.surface: An artist confined to a studio by weak branding ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade name is the name under which a product is sold, i.e. its brand identity.

clue.text: Engineers to get TV adjusted again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
a television is a set

explanation.surface: Engineers called in to retune a television.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set or adjust it once more, here as a past participle.

clue.text: Oppressed by burden, editor held back

indicators.note: in a down answer, the editor pressed down beneath the burden sits after it

parts.note: a burden is the chorus or recurring part of a song, a refrain

explanation.surface: An editor crushed under a heavy workload holds back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burden' looks like a load, but it is the old sense of a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to restrain oneself from acting, so both are past-tense verbs of restraint.

clue.text: Water from river surrounding home

indicators.note: surrounding means the river's name goes round the word for home

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Water drawn from a river that flows round a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is a euphemism for bodily fluid passed by the kidneys, as in 'pass water'.

clue.text: Use evil in a nasty way, being slippery

indicators.note: in a nasty way suggests the letters are mangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone using wickedness cruelly, wriggling out of being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive is hard to grasp or pin down, like a slippery fish or slippery suspect.

clue.text: Elite group open hotel with speech in new development

indicators.note: a new development reshapes what was there, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A hotel opening with a speech at a new property development, attended by the select few.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a group singled out as favoured, originally the Israelites, hence any elite.

clue.text: Once again puts goods on highways, railway being limited

indicators.note: being limited means the railway is boxed in by the highways around it

parts.note: highways are roads
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: Freight shifted back onto roads because rail capacity is limited.
explanation.definitionFit: To reload is to put a load or cargo on again.

clue.text: Female an attraction, one hugged miss

indicators.note: hugged means the numeral is held tight inside the following pair

parts.note: an gives A, the indefinite article
a lure is something that attracts
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An attractive woman embraced someone, yet it went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is an attempt that fails, a flop.

clue.text: Penny, a writer needing to get away, to escape romantically

indicators.note: needing to get away means the writing tool departs from the name

parts.note: Penny is a pet form of the name Penelope
a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: Penny, an author desperate for a break, runs off with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry.

clue.text: Chav tries to rattle ruler's son

indicators.note: to rattle is to shake up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A lout tries to unsettle a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: A chav is British slang for a brash, loutish young person.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsarevich was the eldest son and heir of a Russian tsar.

clue.text: Literary manner, endlessly passionate, in novel

parts.note: thew is an archaic, literary word for manner or custom

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut from the word for passionate

parts.note: ardent means passionate

explanation.surface: A literary style, passionate without end, found in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective but is the definition: Trollope's first Barsetshire novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote this 1855 book, the first of his Barsetshire Chronicles.

clue.text: Stomach problem could be brought by what's sipped, say

indicators.note: could be brought by suggests the letters are reworked to produce something new

explanation.surface: Indigestion that a drink might cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drink causing the ailment; the two words after 'what's' are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical term for indigestion, a gut complaint.

clue.text: Revolutionary ship that ends with mate on board

definitions.text: that ends with mate on board

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A rebel's ship whose voyage ends with a crewmate aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a ship's officer, but it is checkmate on a games board.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game is won by checkmate, so a game of it ends with mate on the board.

clue.text: Exultant cook, chap that's scrambled egg to be eaten

indicators.note: to be eaten means the egg-shaped letter goes inside the rearranged letters
scrambled means the letters of the two words are mixed up

parts.note: an egg is O-shaped, so it gives O

explanation.surface: A delighted cook whose mate has scrambled an egg for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram letters are COCKAHP; 'egg' stands for O because of its shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop means triumphantly delighted, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Police start to explore wooded area

parts.note: cops is slang for police

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Police begin searching a patch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small group of trees, a thicket.

clue.text: Plant giving fuss — hint of blight

parts.note: pother is an old word for a commotion or fuss

indicators.note: hint of means only the initial letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A gardener fussing over a plant that shows a trace of disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is any plant grown for cooking or flavouring, such as parsley.

clue.text: Society learning to avoid a temptation

indicators.note: to avoid means the single letter is shunned and taken out

parts.note: education is learning

explanation.surface: High society learning to steer clear of temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is enticement or allurement, the act of tempting someone.

clue.text: Effective as a policeman

definitions.meaning: a rule that is effective is currently operative or valid
serving in the police service, a member of the force

explanation.surface: Someone praised as being good at police work.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that is effective is operative, and a police officer serves within the police force.

clue.text: Joining cricket side, those people finish getting better

parts.note: the on side (leg side) is one half of a cricket field
them refers to those people
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: Players joining a cricket team finally improve.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means recovering from illness or improving after trouble.

clue.text: Worry about class with idiot lacking style

indicators.note: about means the word for worry goes round the shortened word

parts.note: to eat, as in 'what's eating you?', is to worry

indicators.note: lacking means the letters of the dimwit are taken away

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Fretting that a class with no fool in it lacks flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' looks like the definition but is the wordplay: 'what's eating you?' means what is worrying you.
explanation.definitionFit: Éclat is brilliance of performance or flair, a borrowed word for panache.

clue.text: One was a famous footballer to lose power and energy

parts.note: an engine or battery dies when it loses power
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: An ageing footballer losing strength and stamina.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona was the celebrated Argentine footballer, so the forename identifies him.

clue.text: A story about Fellini's first film

indicators.note: about means the falsehood goes round the director's initial

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the director's name is taken

explanation.surface: A tale concerning the Italian director's debut picture.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1966 British picture starred Michael Caine as a womaniser.

clue.text: Not totally unnecessary items for the drug addict?

indicators.note: not totally means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: Things not quite superfluous for someone injecting drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypodermic syringes are the tools an injecting addict uses, hence the question mark.

clue.text: For example, religious books with a final message that may boost self-esteem

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of religious books
RIP, rest in peace, is the last message on a gravestone

explanation.surface: Scripture with an epitaph intended to flatter someone's self-image.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity pursued mainly to make oneself feel important.

clue.text: Awkward breaths, so rest up where the air has become thinner

definitions.text: where the air has become thinner

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ungainly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A climber gasps for breath, so takes a rest, high where the air is thin.
explanation.definitionFit: This layer of the atmosphere lies just below the stratosphere, at heights where air density has fallen.
